findings.finding: The optional preflight is transactional for timing inputs, causality and timing-record capacity, not for every malformed frame accepted with an explicit duration. A missing WirePayloadBytes field can still fail while constructing the signal after timing.record, Tx state and finishTx scheduling. This gap predates T16 and does not affect validated packet constructors.
findings.recommendation: Keep preflight documentation scoped to timing inputs/capacity. Do not claim arbitrary malformed-frame transactionality or broaden this timing tranche into frame API hardening.

verified_by_inspection: No-argument/default path retains the original arithmetic, physical fields, event insertion order, receive callbacks and RNG calls; extra empty locals have no simulator-state effect.

Explicit continuous computes physical and callback start/end/preamble in the original SignalEngine operand order. Front-end preprocessing is deterministic for retained fixtures and consumes no random streams.

Nanosecond callback targets preserve original physical StartSec, EndSec and PreambleEndSec and therefore retain header/payload allocation formulas. IntervalStartSec is initialized to actual receiver callback Now, matching pinned native BeginReceiveSignal.

Pinned native keeps physical targets and rounds relative callback durations. T16 uses its separately disclosed component-rounding experiment; exact arbitrary-input ns-3 Time equivalence is not claimed.

Optional timing verifies capacity and all receiver plans before timing observations, PHY state, counters or scheduled events. Off-grid receive start before actual TX, nonfinite/negative times, invalid ordering and exact-integer sum overflow are rejected before these mutations.

Physical end bounds remain in interferencePair and closeIntervals. End-callback shifts can alter state/event order as the experiment intends; PHY formulas and physical endpoint comparisons are not silently changed.

Double nanosecond components and guarded sums remain within flintmax; wide frame IDs are retained as uint64 through table construction. Empty and populated timing tables have fixed column types and aligned heights.

Nine prepared MATLAB methods cover input guards, wide identities, exact continuous arithmetic, timing failure before PHY mutation, same/different-rate interference, half duplex, equal-time FIFO, closure accounting, portable-only/single-use injection and actual 20-second NetworkSimulation execution.
limitations: No MATLAB runtime is available in this review; R2025a execution and the default-versus-explicit-continuous integration assertions remain pending owner execution.

Existing nanosecond interference tests check half duplex, callback starts and final accounting. They do not directly assert error-allocation intervals at both sides of a sub-nanosecond physical end boundary. This is a coverage limit, not a detected implementation failure.

The 20-second integration fixture uses the retained routedNetwork closure delegate; it covers actual stack/PHY execution and application generation but does not prove completed discovery, end-to-end delivery or the full-geometry benchmark outcome.
